books.headline: THE EXACT TIME
books.hook: you are born in one exact second, room and set of physical circumstances that demand a complete book.
books.title: The Exact Time
passage: The book records your arrival with absurd precision: the exact second, the length of the pregnancy, the temperature in the room, the light across every surface, the people present and the positions of their bodies.
It preserves how you were positioned, which part of you appeared first, how long it took you to draw breath and the volume of that first breath.
Change one degree, one gesture or a fraction of a second and another birth occurs.
And for that nearly identical birth, the Library needs another complete book.
books.aftertaste: Another birth. Another complete book.

neighbors.difference: You are born four seconds later and nothing else changes.
The place, date and every other possible circumstance of birth change.

books.headline: FOUR SECONDS
books.title: Four Seconds
passage: The adjacent book is identical to yours except for four seconds. You are born four seconds later. No one notices. The doctor does not change position. Your mother breathes the same way. Outside, the same cars move through the same rain. Throughout your life, everything happens in exactly the same way, but every age begins four seconds later. Even your death keeps the same date and place. The Library needs another complete book to preserve that useless delay.
books.aftertaste: Four seconds need another book.

neighbors.difference: The birth occurs in your exact circumstances.
The place, date and every other possible circumstance of birth change.

books.headline: EVERY ROOM
books.title: Every Room
passage: There are books in which you are born in every hospital, house, vehicle, shelter and open space where your birth could have taken place. Others change the country, the weather or the people present. Then come every date, every length of pregnancy and every body you could have been born with. Each birth requires a complete life to follow it. There is no single shelf for your beginnings. There are entire corridors, and in each book you are born only once.
books.aftertaste: In each book, you are born only once.

neighbors.difference: The birth occurs in your exact circumstances.
You are born four seconds later and nothing else changes.

books.headline: THE HOUSE YOU REMEMBER
books.hook: every bedroom, school, game and fear from your childhood is recorded so that you can be written without omission.
books.title: The House You Remember
passage: One book contains your exact childhood: every bedroom, every journey to school, every abandoned game, every fear you never shared. It preserves the repeated mornings that now blur together and the words adults spoke that you did not understand then. It also preserves everything that came afterwards. The person reading this sentence began there, among days that seemed interchangeable and that the Library had to record one by one in order to write you without leaving anything out.
books.aftertaste: The Library recorded every interchangeable day.

neighbors.difference: Another childhood converges on this same afternoon.
A different desk leads to an unrecognisable person.

books.headline: ANOTHER CHILDHOOD, THIS SAME AFTERNOON
books.title: Another Childhood, This Same Afternoon
passage: In another book, you grow up in another house, learn in different classrooms and become friends with people you never meet in this life. Your family follows different routines. You fear other things. Yet decades later, you reach this same afternoon with the same job, wearing the same clothes and about to say the same sentence. Two incompatible childhoods have produced this almost identical minute. The books do not meet here. They remain separate until their final pages.
books.aftertaste: The two childhoods do not meet.

neighbors.difference: The childhood matches the one you remember exactly.
A different desk leads to an unrecognisable person.

books.headline: THE NEXT DESK
books.title: The Next Desk
passage: Two books match throughout your early years. The same family, the same bedroom, the same streets. In one, you are assigned the desk beside the window; in the other, the desk in the next row. Nothing important happens that day. After that, your friendships, habits and education slowly change, along with the cities where you will live and the people who will recognise your voice. Before the second book reaches its halfway point, it describes someone you would not recognise as yourself.
books.aftertaste: The second book no longer resembles you.

neighbors.difference: The childhood matches the one you remember exactly.
Another childhood converges on this same afternoon.

books.headline: THE FIRST LANGUAGE
books.hook: every word you say belongs to one of the languages you could have learned.
books.title: The First Language
passage: There is a book containing every word you have spoken in the language in which you learned to ask for water, say no, joke and call your family by name. It records your mistakes before anything you said correctly. It preserves expressions you repeated for years and a final sentence you do not yet know. That language does more than fill your conversations: it determines which sounds you distinguish, what you call things and which words will fail you when you need them most.
books.aftertaste: Your final sentence also belongs to that language.

neighbors.difference: The same declaration is spoken in another language.
All the languages you could understand are combined.

books.headline: THE SAME SENTENCE
books.title: The Same Sentence
passage: There are books in which you make the same statement in every language you could have learned. With each language, the childhood needed to master it changes, along with the country, the school, the conversations that came before and the person able to understand you. Sometimes the sentence has the same effect. Sometimes it sounds awkward, formal or ambiguous, or cannot be translated without adding something. For you to say those few words differently, the Library replaces thousands of pages of your life.
books.aftertaste: A few words replace thousands of pages.

neighbors.difference: The life unfolds in your first language.
All the languages you could understand are combined.

books.headline: EVERYTHING YOU COULD UNDERSTAND
books.title: Everything You Could Understand
passage: One shelf contains the lives in which you speak one language; the next, two; then come all the possible combinations. In some books, you argue with your family in one language and work in another. In others, you think, count, insult, love and die using different words. Every language combines with every country, education, profession and relationship. There is no translation of your life. There are complete books for every way you could name it.
books.aftertaste: There is no translation of your life.

neighbors.difference: The life unfolds in your first language.
The same declaration is spoken in another language.

books.headline: YOUR WORKING DAY
books.hook: every working day, job and possible sequence of jobs occupies a complete life.
books.title: Your Working Day
passage: This book contains every day you spend working: the first task you learned, the wasted hours, the mistakes without consequence, the journeys, the breaks and the last time you will close a door at the end of a shift. It also records the jobs that lasted briefly and those that shaped decades. Your profession fits into a short answer. The life behind that answer fills thousands of pages with schedules, tired bodies, repeated conversations and mornings when you began again.
books.aftertaste: Your profession occupies thousands of pages.

neighbors.difference: Completely different careers converge at eight fifteen.
Every job and the order in which you do them change.

books.headline: AT EIGHT FIFTEEN
books.title: At Eight Fifteen
passage: In one book, you work in a hospital your whole life. In another, you change occupations twenty times. In another, you spend years unemployed; in another, you work nights in a factory, on a ship or at a job that does not yet have a name. All those books contain an evening when you arrive home at eight fifteen, put down your keys and drink a glass of water. The careers are nothing alike. That minute is.
books.aftertaste: At eight fifteen, the careers converge.

neighbors.difference: The book preserves the exact sequence of your working days.
Every job and the order in which you do them change.

books.headline: ALL YOUR JOBS
books.title: All Your Jobs
passage: There is a book for every job you could do and another for every possible order of jobs: farm before office, laboratory after warehouse, retirement followed by a return, a single profession for sixty years. Some tasks change your body. Others change only how you spend eight hours a day. The Library does not separate vocations from forgettable jobs. Every working day counts, and every sequence requires your entire life to be written again.
books.aftertaste: Each sequence writes your life again.

neighbors.difference: The book preserves the exact sequence of your working days.
Completely different careers converge at eight fifteen.

books.headline: WHERE YOU SLEEP
books.hook: every room, home, city and possible sequence of moves demands another book.
books.title: Where You Sleep
passage: There is a book for the life in which you sleep tonight in your exact room. It records the distance between the bed and the wall, what you see from the window and the objects you can reach without getting up. That room appears during one stretch of your book and then disappears. Yet sleeping there changes the complete list of places you have called home. The book preserves them all, even those you could no longer walk through from memory.
books.aftertaste: The room is also part of the book.

neighbors.difference: Only the room for one night changes.
All possible homes and sequences of addresses change.

books.headline: THE NEXT ROOM
books.title: The Next Room
passage: The book beside it changes only which room you sleep in for one night. It is in the same building, beneath the same roof, a few metres from your own. You sleep for the same length of time and wake with no memory of anything different. The rest of your life matches word for word. Even so, one book says your body spent that night on one side of the corridor; the other says it was on the other side. They cannot occupy the same book.
books.aftertaste: One night on the other side of the corridor.

neighbors.difference: You sleep in the exact sequence of rooms you know.
Every possible home and sequence of addresses changes.

books.headline: ALL YOUR ADDRESSES
books.title: All Your Addresses
passage: There are books for every flat, house, room, city and view you could have. Then come the sequences: three moves, none, forty; a childhood in one place and old age in another; decades facing the same window. Changing an address alters the nearby shops, the stairs you use and the faces you meet when you leave. The Library contains every complete sequence of homes, including the one in which you never inhabit any of the places you now remember.
books.aftertaste: Every address contains a complete life.

neighbors.difference: You sleep in the exact sequence of rooms you know.
Only the room for one night changes.

books.headline: THOSE WHO APPEAR
books.hook: all the children you could have appear, along with every complete person who never begins here.
books.title: Those Who Appear
passage: This book records whether you have children, how many, with whom and in what order they arrive. It describes their bodies, temperaments, illnesses, words and lives after yours ends. If you have none, it also records that absence throughout all your years. One number on one page determines hundreds of people you know, rooms occupied, meals prepared and dates remembered. The book does not treat that number as a detail.
books.aftertaste: One number changes all those pages.

neighbors.difference: Conception occurs an instant earlier and another person appears.
Every possible child appears in every order and number.

books.headline: AN INSTANT EARLIER
books.title: An Instant Earlier
passage: In the adjacent book, conception occurs an instant earlier. Everything seems the same: the place, the two people, the day. Yet another body is born. The person who appears there will have a voice, a face and a complete life. In your book, they do not die or disappear: they simply never begin. Around both books are countless variations of that instant, and each introduces someone different who will live through pages that do not exist here.
books.aftertaste: Another person begins in that instant.

neighbors.difference: The exact configuration of children in this life appears.
Every possible child appears in every order and number.

books.headline: THE ABSENT POPULATION
books.title: The Absent Population
passage: One section of the Library contains all the children you could have with every person, on every date, in every order and number. Some share almost everything; others could not recognise one another. Their lives combine with their friendships, partners, jobs and descendants. None is a draft of another. Each occupies a book where they are as real and ordinary as you are in this one. Most of those complete people will not appear once in your exact book.
books.aftertaste: Most of them do not appear in your book.

neighbors.difference: The exact configuration of children in this life appears.
Conception occurs an instant earlier and another person appears.

books.headline: BEFORE YOU
books.hook: the possible lives of your parents change the conditions of yours again and again.
books.title: Before You
passage: Your book begins before you can remember. It contains the decisions, jobs, illnesses and movements of your parents that made your exact birth possible. It records who they were before they became your parents and how they continued to have lives of their own as you grew up. Every change in their lives alters the conditions of yours: a city, a schedule, a conversation, the day they crossed paths. To describe you completely, the book needs pages in which you do not yet exist.
books.aftertaste: Your book needs pages from before you.

neighbors.difference: The same parents live differently.
One or both of the people who are your parents change.

books.headline: THE SAME PARENTS
books.title: The Same Parents
passage: There are books in which your parents are the same people, but live differently. They keep their bodies and names; they change jobs, homes, beliefs, friendships or countries.
Sometimes you are born on the same date. Sometimes years later. In some books your life ends up almost identical to this one, though you reach it by a completely different family history.
Each of those variations needs another complete book for you.
books.aftertaste: The same parents. Another complete book.

neighbors.difference: The book preserves the exact lives of your parents before you.
One or both of the people who are your parents change.

books.headline: OTHER NAMES BEFORE YOURS
books.title: Other Names Before Yours
passage: Farther away are the books in which one of your parents changes, and then both. People you do not know today are your parents in those books.
With each pair, your childhood, your body, your family and everything that follows all change. In some you keep the name you have now, or the same date of birth; in others those change too.
For every possible pair there exist, once again, all the books of the lives you could live as their child.
books.aftertaste: Other parents. Other complete books.

neighbors.difference: The book preserves the exact lives of your parents before you.
The same parents live differently.

books.headline: WHAT YOU KEEP
books.hook: the same events produce every possible combination of memories kept, distorted and lost.
books.title: What You Keep
passage: There is a book containing the exact events of your life and the part you still remember. It distinguishes between them. It records afternoons that happened and that you can no longer recover, faces whose names you lost and sentences you believe you remember incorrectly. It also keeps insignificant memories that survived for no visible reason. Your past occupies the book once as event and again as memory. The two versions begin to separate long before you notice the difference.
books.aftertaste: The past happened once and you remember it another way.

neighbors.difference: Only the memory of one childhood afternoon remains.
Every combination of memory and forgetting changes.

books.headline: THE REMAINING AFTERNOON
books.title: The Remaining Afternoon
passage: In one book, you reach old age remembering a single afternoon from your childhood. It was not decisive: a table, a drink, light on a wall. Everything else happened just as it did in your life, but it is no longer available to you. Even so, you continue to use skills you no longer remember learning and to recognise places without knowing why. The book contains all those decades. You, inside it, retain only a few minutes.
books.aftertaste: The book keeps decades. You keep a few minutes.

neighbors.difference: The events and memories match those of this life.
Every combination of memory and forgetting changes.

books.headline: EVERY WAY TO FORGET
books.title: Every Way to Forget
passage: There are books with the same events and different memories. In one, you remember every room; in another, none. A face remains, a date shifts, a conversation loses a word. Then come all the combinations: the exact, the incomplete, the distorted and the lost. Nothing supernatural occurs. Time, attention, age and the body do their ordinary work. For every possible way of remembering the same life, the Library needs to write another complete book.
books.aftertaste: The same life needs another memory.

neighbors.difference: The events and memories match those of this life.
Only the memory of one childhood afternoon remains.

books.headline: INVENTORY
books.hook: every object you could own, even for a few minutes, demands another complete life.
books.title: Inventory
passage: Your book includes every object that ever belonged to you: keys, shoes, phones, furniture, photographs, receipts and books. It records how long each stayed with you, where you left it and whether it still exists. Some objects occupy decades; others, an afternoon. Almost none deserves a scene. Together they form an unrepeatable sequence of things touched, kept, lent, broken and discarded. To copy your life exactly, the Library cannot omit even the object you forgot that same day.
books.aftertaste: The Library omits no object.

neighbors.difference: A blue paper clip belongs to you for seventeen minutes.
Every object and every sequence of acquisition and loss changes.

books.headline: THE BLUE PAPER CLIP
books.title: The Blue Paper Clip
passage: The adjacent book differs by one blue paper clip. You find it on a table, put it in a pocket and throw it away seventeen minutes later. It serves no purpose. No one sees it. It changes no decision, conversation or memory. Every other page matches your exact life. Yet for seventeen minutes you own something that was never yours here. That insignificant difference requires everything from birth to death to be repeated.
books.aftertaste: Seventeen minutes demand a complete book.

neighbors.difference: You own the exact sequence of objects from this life.
Every object and every sequence of acquisition and loss changes.

books.headline: ALL YOUR THINGS
books.title: All Your Things
passage: On one shelf, one object changes at a time. On the next, two; then a hundred; then all of them. There are lives with rooms full of things and lives in which almost nothing bears your name. Every car combines with every key; every photograph with every home; every garment with every day on which you could wear it. Then come all the sequences of acquisition and loss. The Library contains inventories that cannot be finished because each inventory is embedded in a complete life.
books.aftertaste: Every inventory is inside a life.

neighbors.difference: You own the exact sequence of objects from this life.
A blue paper clip belongs to you for seventeen minutes.

books.headline: WHERE YOU WENT
books.hook: every possible step, journey and encounter is placed precisely within your life.
books.title: Where You Went
passage: There is a book that preserves all your movements through space. Every pavement, staircase, road, corridor, flight and doorway appears in the exact order in which you encountered it. It includes the journeys you repeated until you stopped noticing them and the last step you took before reading this sentence. Your life does not merely connect important places. It is made of millions of positions in between that you never named and that the book must specify in order to place you where you actually were.
books.aftertaste: The book specifies where you were.

neighbors.difference: A single step lands twenty centimetres to the left.
Every route and the people encountered along it change.

books.headline: TWENTY CENTIMETRES
books.title: Twenty Centimetres
passage: The next book places one of your steps twenty centimetres to the left. You do not stumble. You meet no one. Your destination, your arrival time and the rest of your life remain the same. Only the sole of your foot touches another piece of ground for less than a second. The change vanishes immediately, but it cannot be erased from the record. The Library rewrites every page for a life that strayed only the width of a hand.
books.aftertaste: The width of a hand rewrites every page.

neighbors.difference: Every movement follows the exact route of this life.
Every route and the people encountered along it change.

books.headline: EVERY CROSSING
books.title: Every Crossing
passage: There are books for every route between the places in your life and for every possible order of places. Then each route combines with the people who could travel it at the same time. One corner contains encounters that last for decades and brief encounters neither person remembers. A corridor may be empty when you cross it, or contain anyone who could have reached it. Every step opens not one alternative but corridors of books in which the path, the time and every body present change together.
books.aftertaste: Every step opens entire corridors.

neighbors.difference: Every movement follows the exact route of this life.
A single step lands twenty centimetres to the left.

books.headline: YOUR EXACT LIFE
books.hook: your exact life is already written from birth to the circumstances of your death.
books.title: Your Book
passage: There is a book containing your exact life. Its first page gives the date, time and place of your birth. Then come every home, every meal, every conversation and every day you have forgotten.
One page describes how you have come to read these words. The pages after it contain the time you will wake tomorrow, the first object you will touch and the words you will say before leaving.
The final page gives the exact date, time, place and circumstances of your death.
books.aftertaste: The complete book already exists.

neighbors.difference: The same life ends one second later.
Tomorrow you take thirteen steps to the kitchen instead of twelve.

books.headline: ONE SECOND MORE
books.title: One Second More
passage: This book matches yours from birth until the final day. It contains the same people, the same rooms and every one of the same words.
Only the time printed on the final page changes.
Here, you die one second later.
books.aftertaste: One second needs another book.

neighbors.difference: The final page ends one second earlier.
Your death does not change, but tomorrow you take one more step.

books.headline: THIRTEEN STEPS
books.title: Thirteen Steps
passage: This book matches yours in every detail except for one thing tomorrow.
From the bed to the kitchen, in this book you take thirteen steps instead of twelve. Nothing else changes: not breakfast, not the years after it, not the circumstances of your death.
That single step is enough for another complete book to exist.
books.aftertaste: One different step. Another complete book.

neighbors.difference: Tomorrow you take twelve steps to the kitchen.
The life matches, except the final page ends one second later.

books.headline: THE FAMILY OPPOSITE
books.hook: you are born into the family across from your home, and your current family simply lives nearby.
books.title: The Door Opposite
passage: There is a book in which you were born into the family living opposite your home. Their parents are your parents. Their children are your siblings.
You grew up in their rooms, ate at their table and learned to speak with their words. The home where you grew up in this life belongs to another family.
Sometimes you pass on the stairs the people who, here, are your family. In that book they are only your neighbours, and you greet them as you go by.
books.aftertaste: Your family lives opposite.

neighbors.difference: You are born behind every possible door on your street.
Someone else occupies your room in your current family.

books.headline: EVERY DOOR
books.title: Every Door
passage: There is a book in which you were born behind every door on your street.
In one you are an only child. In another you share a room with three siblings. In another, the person you now call your sister lives two buildings away and never learns your name.
Every door contains a complete childhood.
books.aftertaste: Every door contains a childhood.

neighbors.difference: You are born into the family living opposite your home.
Your current family remains at home, but another child takes your place.

books.headline: YOUR ROOM WITHOUT YOU
books.title: Your Room Without You
passage: In this book your current family lives in the same home. They keep the same jobs, the same meals and almost all the same photographs.
Another child sleeps in your room, takes your place at the table and calls your parents Mum and Dad.
You grow up somewhere else. Neither family notices an absence.
books.aftertaste: Neither family notices an absence.

neighbors.difference: You are born into the family living opposite your home.
You are born behind every possible door on your street.

books.headline: EVERY POSSIBLE SEAT
books.hook: you die in an aircraft accident. There is a different book for every possible seat, every age and every route.
books.title: Every Seat
passage: There is a book in which you die in an aircraft accident sitting in 1A. Another in 1B. Another in 1C. And so on: a different book for every possible seat.

Each seat combines with every aircraft, airline, airport, destination, route, altitude, delay and weather condition. In some books you die at six months. In others, at seventeen, at fifty-two or at one hundred and ten.
Every combination requires another complete book, with your whole life from birth to that flight.
books.aftertaste: A different seat. Another whole book.

neighbors.difference: The same sequence exists for every ordinary way of dying.
The whole life matches until the final minute.

books.headline: EVERY WAY
books.title: Every Way
passage: Then come the books in which you die on trains, buses, in cars, on bicycles and aboard ships.
There are also books in which you die walking, swimming, dancing, eating, sleeping or working. For each activity, the age, place, time and people present all change.
In every book you are born again on the first page.
books.aftertaste: In every book you are born again.

neighbors.difference: Only the flights, seats, routes and ages change.
The lives remain identical until the final minute.

books.headline: THE SAME FINAL MINUTE
books.title: Until the Final Minute
passage: These books match throughout your life.
Same family. Same body. Same meals, jobs, conversations and journeys. They arrive together at the final minute.
Afterwards only your death changes: in one book it is an illness, in another an accident, in another you end it yourself.
books.aftertaste: In each book, you die in another way.

neighbors.difference: Every seat, flight, age and route produces another complete life.
The activity, place and people present all change too.

books.headline: LEFT FIRST
books.hook: you put on your left sock first every day of your adult life, and nothing else changes.
books.title: Left First
passage: In this book you put on your left sock first every day of your adult life.
The order changes no conversation, job or relationship. You reach the same places at the same time. You die on the same day.
From eighteen until the end, the left goes first.
books.aftertaste: The left goes first until the end.

neighbors.difference: One Tuesday, at forty-six, you put on the right sock first.
You put on the right sock first every day of your adult life.

books.headline: ONE TUESDAY
books.title: One Tuesday
passage: This book matches the previous one throughout your life except for one morning.
One Tuesday, at forty-six, you put on your right sock first. You do not notice. Nobody sees.
The rest of the book matches again through its final word.
books.aftertaste: One morning needs another book.

neighbors.difference: The left sock goes first on that Tuesday too.
The right sock goes first every day, not just once.

books.headline: RIGHT EVERY TIME
books.title: Right Every Time
passage: Here you put on your right sock first from eighteen until your death.
Everything else remains the same: the people you love, the illnesses, the homes, the sentences and the length of your life.
It takes another whole book.
books.aftertaste: It takes another whole book.

neighbors.difference: The left sock goes first every day.
The right goes first on only one Tuesday.

books.headline: WHAT WAS SAID
books.hook: every possible word, pause and silence occupies its own complete book.
books.title: What Was Said
passage: Your book records every sound you have uttered: the first syllables, repeated questions, automatic answers, names, arguments and words you said when no one was listening. It also contains all your silences, with their exact duration. Some sentences changed a relationship. Most changed nothing. The Library writes both with the same care because an exact life cannot replace one forgettable word with another, or one second of silence with one second of speech.
books.aftertaste: One silent second is not equal to one second of speech.

neighbors.difference: One pause lasts a second longer and nothing else changes.
Every possible word, pause and conversation changes.

books.headline: A LONGER PAUSE
books.title: A Longer Pause
passage: In the book beside it, you take one additional second to answer a question. Then you say exactly the same thing. The other person waits. Nothing changes: not their interpretation, not the conversation that follows, not the day. Decades later, both books reach the same ending. They differ only in that slightly longer silence. One contains a life with that pause. The other, a life without it. The Library does not decide that they are equivalent.
books.aftertaste: The Library preserves that pause.

neighbors.difference: Every word and every silence match exactly.
Every possible word, pause and conversation changes.

books.headline: EVERYTHING YOU COULD SAY
books.title: Everything You Could Say
passage: One word changes; then a syllable; then the order of two sentences. There are books for every conversation you could have and for every sentence you would never say. Each version combines with every voice, pause and silence of everyone else. Most disappear without consequence. Some words change jobs, families or countries. The books are not ordered by importance. Beside a life transformed by one sentence are millions that differ only in sounds no one remembered.
books.aftertaste: The books are not ordered by importance.

neighbors.difference: Every word and every silence match exactly.
One pause lasts a second longer and nothing else changes.

books.headline: YOUR NIGHTS
books.hook: every possible night changes its bed, position, awakening, dream or companion.
books.title: Your Nights
passage: There is a book containing every night of your life. It records when you went to bed, which side you slept on, how many times you woke and who breathed nearby. It preserves the dreams you remembered and those that vanished before you opened your eyes. For years, its nighttime pages seem to repeat: the same bed, the same darkness, the same motionless body. But no two nights occupy exactly the same hours or leave you equally tired the next day.
books.aftertaste: No night occupies the same hours.

neighbors.difference: For one night, you sleep facing the other way.
Every bed, position, interruption and companion changes.

books.headline: FACING THE OTHER WAY
books.title: Facing the Other Way
passage: The adjacent book preserves your entire waking life. The same decisions, words, journeys and relationships. Only your position during one night changes: you sleep facing the wall instead of the room. You do not remember it in the morning. It affects neither your body nor the following day. The difference exists only while you are unaware of it. To preserve it, the Library also duplicates every page on which you are awake.
books.aftertaste: The difference exists while you do not know it.

neighbors.difference: Every night matches the one in this life.
Every bed, position, interruption and companion changes.

books.headline: EVERY BED
books.title: Every Bed
passage: There are books in which every one of your nights takes place in another room, another country, beside another person or in an empty bed. There are lives with decades of interrupted sleep and others in which you always wake at the same time. Then come all the combinations of positions, awakenings, dreams and forgetting. Some change your days. Others remain sealed inside the night. Even differences you never come to know occupy complete books bearing your name.
books.aftertaste: Every night occupies another book.

neighbors.difference: Every night matches the one in this life.
For one night, you sleep facing the other way.

books.headline: EVERY POSSIBLE BODY
books.hook: you are born with every body you could have had, and each one needs a complete life.
books.title: Every Body
passage: There are books in which you are born on the same day, to the same parents and in the same room, with every body you could have had.
Height, face, sex, voice, strength, mobility and health all change. Every body ages in every way available to it.
None ends with a description. They all need a complete life.
books.aftertaste: Every body reaches its final page.

neighbors.difference: Two bodies differ by only one millimetre of adult height.
Every bodily trait combines with every other one.

books.headline: ONE MILLIMETRE MORE
books.title: One Millimetre
passage: Two of those books match in every respect: your family, your face, your health and every event in your life.
In one, you grow to be one millimetre taller as an adult. The difference appears as you grow and remains until your death.
A whole book for that millimetre.
books.aftertaste: A whole book for that millimetre.

neighbors.difference: Height is only one of all the traits that change.
The millimetre combines with every voice, face, health and family.

books.headline: EVERY COMBINATION
books.title: Every Combination
passage: For every height there are all the voices. For every voice, all the faces. For every face, all the illnesses, injuries, abilities and ways of ageing.
Then each of those bodies lives with every family, in every city, beside every person it could meet.
In one book you have your present body.
books.aftertaste: In one book you have this body.

neighbors.difference: Every possible body receives a complete life.
Two of those bodies differ by only one millimetre.

books.headline: THERE IS ALREADY A BOOK IN WHICH...
books.hook: you spend your whole life travelling the world by car.
books.title: Every Road
passage: There is a book in which you spend your whole life travelling by car.
Each morning you wake in a different place. You drive for hours, through cities, back roads, mountain passes, deserts, coastlines and villages you will never see again.
At nightfall you park, eat, sleep and the following day you drive once more.
You never reach a final destination.
You travel every place a road can take you.
And you are happy.
books.aftertaste: Every possible road can hold an entire life.

neighbors.difference: The same life in motion, but on two wheels.
The same need to keep moving, but through the sky.

books.headline: IN THE ADJACENT BOOK...
books.title: Every Bicycle
passage: In the adjacent book you do the same thing by bicycle.
You cross the same countries more slowly. Some roads vanish and paths appear that the car could never follow.
You sleep wherever the day ends. You wake and pedal again.
Your body ages on the bicycle. Your legs change, your speed changes and the distance you can cover in a day grows shorter.
But you never stop moving forward.
Here, too, you are happy.
books.aftertaste: The world changes when the speed of your life changes.

neighbors.difference: Here you swap the bicycle for a car and travel every road again.
Here you leave the ground and continue the journey by air.

books.headline: IN ANOTHER BOOK...
books.title: Every Sky
passage: In another book you spend your life travelling by aeroplane.
Each day you fly somewhere new. The airports change, the airlines, the seats, the routes, the layovers and the people sitting beside you.
You land, sleep for a few hours and take off again.
Over a complete lifetime you see from above the cities that in other books you cross by car or bicycle.
You never decide to stay.
And you never need to.
books.aftertaste: A life can have no final place and still be complete.

neighbors.difference: Here you return to the ground and travel the world by road.
Here you cross the same world far more slowly, by bicycle.

books.headline: THE EXACT AGE
books.hook: there is a different book for every exact age at which you could die.
books.title: The Exact Age
passage: There is a book in which you die at 52 years, 3 months, 11 days, 7 hours, 14 minutes and 8 seconds.
In another you die one second later.
In another, ten years earlier.
For every possible age there is another complete book, containing the whole life that had to happen first for you to reach exactly that instant.
books.aftertaste: Another age. Another complete book.

neighbors.difference: The life ends at every age and after every possible final day.
After the final night, you live one more day.

books.headline: EVERY DURATION
books.title: Every Duration
passage: There are books that end after a few minutes and books that pass through a childhood, an adult life or extreme old age. For every duration, there are all possible final days: ordinary, busy, quiet, shared, unnoticed. The Library does not reserve the ending for an extraordinary scene. It may arrive after you wash your hands, look at a street or set a cup on a table. Every age reached contains countless complete lives capable of ending there.
books.aftertaste: Every age contains countless lives.

neighbors.difference: The life ends at your exact age.
After the final night, you live one more day.

books.headline: ONE MORE DAY
books.title: One More Day
passage: Two books describe the same life until your final night. In one, it ends. In another, you wake and live one additional day with nothing exceptional in it: you get up, eat, speak, wait. A third book adds another day. Then come weeks, years and decades, each with all its possible contents. There is no single continuation. From any age, the Library preserves every amount of time remaining and every life that can fit inside it.
books.aftertaste: Another day. Then all the others.

neighbors.difference: The life ends at your exact age.
The life ends at every age and after every possible final day.

books.headline: YOUR FULL NAME
books.hook: you keep your name while your body, family, language, memories and everything else change.
books.title: Your Full Name
passage: This book preserves your name and everything that currently goes with it: body, family, country, language, memories, habits and relationships. Whenever someone says it, they are referring to the exact accumulation of those pages. Yet the name takes up very little space. It could easily be copied onto the cover of another book. The Library does so. Open that other book, and you find the same name and none of the circumstances that taught you to recognise it.
books.aftertaste: The same name fits on another cover.

neighbors.difference: The same signature belongs to a completely different life.
Completely different people answer to your same name.

books.headline: THE SAME SIGNATURE
books.title: The Same Signature
passage: There is a book in which your signature is exactly the same as it is here, but your hand has a different shape. You were born in another country, speak another language and belong to another family. Your education, work, beliefs and memories are different. You have never seen the places you now call yours. Even so, the signature at the bottom of certain documents carries exactly the same name. Everything you are has changed around those letters, and the letters continue to claim that the book is about you.
books.aftertaste: The letters keep saying that you are you.

neighbors.difference: Your name keeps everything it currently means.
Completely different people answer to your same name.

books.headline: EVERYONE UNDER YOUR NAME
books.title: Everyone Under Your Name
passage: An entire section repeats your name on its spines. Inside, the bodies, ages, parents, languages, professions, habits and deaths change. Some books retain a single recognisable trait. Others retain none. There are books in which completely different people respond when someone says those same syllables. The Library does not mark the point at which you cease to be you. It simply aligns the books and lets your name remain fixed while replacing everything it ever meant.
books.aftertaste: Your name remains. Everything else changes.

neighbors.difference: Your name keeps everything it currently means.
The same signature belongs to a completely different life.

books.headline: ONLY THE GESTURE REMAINS
books.hook: everything changes except one gesture, meal or word that remains exactly the same.
books.title: Only the Gesture Remains
passage: There is a book in which almost nothing from your present life remains. Another body, another family, another country, another language, another job and another death. You know none of the people who make up your days here. Yet at the same age, you make exactly one gesture that you made in this life: you move a chair aside with your hand before sitting down. The position of your fingers, the force and the duration match. The whole book seems foreign except for that precise second.
books.aftertaste: Only that second is still yours.

neighbors.difference: Two different lives share one exact breakfast.
Everything changes except the final word.

books.headline: THE SAME BREAKFAST
books.title: The Same Breakfast
passage: Two lives have different births, faces, educations, cities, beliefs and relationships. Their pages never draw close again. But on a particular date, you eat the same breakfast, in the same order, in the same quantities and for the same number of minutes. Afterwards, the books separate again until two different deaths. Among thousands of differences, that identical meal is harder to ignore than any change. The Library preserves it without drawing attention to it.
books.aftertaste: The Library does not single out the breakfast.

neighbors.difference: Everything changes except one exact gesture.
Everything changes except the final word.

books.headline: THE LAST WORD
books.title: The Last Word
passage: There are books in which everything changes except your final word. You reach it with another voice, after a life you do not recognise, surrounded by people you will never know here. In some books, you say it in another language, but the final sound matches. In others, it means something different. Bodies, families, countries and entire decades are replaced to lead to the same brief utterance. What remains constant no longer seems like a foundation. It seems like the detail that cannot be removed.
books.aftertaste: The final word remains.

neighbors.difference: Everything changes except one exact gesture.
Two different lives share one exact breakfast.

books.headline: EVERY LIVING PERSON
books.hook: you share your life with every person alive today whom it would have been possible to meet.
books.title: Every Living Person
passage: There are books in which you share your life with every person alive today you could possibly have met.
In some you marry. In others you are friends for sixty years, raise a family, work together or stop speaking.
Many of those people will never enter your present life.
Right now they live somewhere without knowing who you are.
books.aftertaste: But in some book, their life is joined to yours.

neighbors.difference: Every possible relationship exists with each person.
Every possible relationship combines into complete networks.

books.headline: EVERY RELATIONSHIP
books.title: Every Relationship
passage: For every person who has ever existed or who exists in the world, there are books in which your lives come to coincide and you have every possible relationship.
The same person can be your partner, your closest friend, the one who hires you, the one who cares for you, the one who harms you or someone with whom you merely share a queue.
Then each of those relationships exists again with every possible duration: a few minutes, several years or an entire life.
books.aftertaste: With the same person, any relationship can exist.

neighbors.difference: Every possible person shares a complete life with you.
Every relationship combines with every other relationship.

books.headline: THE WHOLE NETWORK
books.title: The Whole Network
passage: Changing one person is not enough.
For every possible partner there are all the possible friends. For every group of friends, all the colleagues, neighbours, doctors, teachers and strangers who could affect you.
Every combination forms a different life around you.
books.aftertaste: Every combination forms another life.

neighbors.difference: Every living person appears in every possible bond with you.
One person occupies every possible role.

books.headline: WHAT NO ONE SAW
books.hook: your visible life remains identical while the thoughts, desires and interpretations it contains change.
books.title: What No One Saw
passage: This book reproduces your observable life without changing anything.
You are born in the same second, inhabit the same homes, say the same words and make the same gestures. Your job, relationships, journeys, illnesses and death remain the same.
Two people watching both lives from outside would not find a single difference.
But as you perform each action, you think other things, desire other outcomes and interpret what happens differently.
The Library needs two complete books because inwardly you did not live the same life.
books.aftertaste: Inwardly, you did not live the same life.

neighbors.difference: One thought appears for three seconds and changes nothing.
Every inner interpretation, intention and combination changes.

books.headline: ONE THOUGHT LESS
books.title: One Thought Less
passage: As you lift a glass, a brief sentence appears in your mind.
You do not say it. It changes neither your expression, the movement of your hand nor what you do next. Three seconds later, you have forgotten it.
In the adjacent book, that sentence never forms.
Everything visible matches, as does every earlier and later thought until your death.
For three seconds, one life contains something the other does not.
To preserve that inaccessible difference, the Library writes both of them again in full.
books.aftertaste: Three seconds need two books.

neighbors.difference: The visible life matches, but the inner experience changes.
Every inner interpretation, intention and combination changes.

books.headline: ALL THE LIVES INSIDE YOU
books.title: All the Lives Inside You
passage: There are books for every thought you could have while hearing the same sentence, every memory prompted by the same smell and every fear you never express.
In some, you act from affection; in others, from habit, calculation, shame or exhaustion. The gesture remains identical.
Then come all the combinations: what you desire, what you suspect, what you pay attention to, what you ignore and every sentence you form without speaking it.
From outside, your life does not change.
Inside, the Library does not end.
books.aftertaste: Inside, the Library does not end.

neighbors.difference: The visible life matches, but the inner experience changes.
One thought appears for three seconds and changes nothing.

books.headline: ONE THING, THEN ALL OF THEM
books.hook: every city combines with every job, every home and every person with whom you could share it.
books.title: One Thing, Then All of Them
passage: First come the books in which you live in every possible city.
For every city there are all the jobs. For every job, all the homes. For every home, all the people with whom you could share it.
No possibility replaces the one before it. Each combines with all the others.
books.aftertaste: Every possibility combines with the others.

neighbors.difference: Even one Tuesday contains all its possible combinations.
Family, body, language and every other detail all change at once.

books.headline: A SINGLE TUESDAY
books.title: A Single Tuesday
passage: Even if your family, body, home and job stay fixed, every possible Tuesday remains.
Every time you could wake. Every breakfast. Every route. Every person you could cross paths with. Every word you could say and every word you could leave unsaid.
Then come all the combinations among those differences within a single day.
books.aftertaste: All those differences fit inside one Tuesday.

neighbors.difference: The combination begins with cities, jobs, homes and people.
Every category of your life changes at once.

books.headline: YOUR BOOK AMONG THEM
books.title: Your Book Among Them
passage: Now family, body, language, city, home, job, partner, children, health, habits and age at death all change at once.
Every combination divides again for every meal, journey, sentence, gesture, object and second.
Among all those books, one matches you exactly.
books.aftertaste: One matches you exactly.

neighbors.difference: The possibilities combine one category at a time.
The combination is limited to a single Tuesday.

books.headline: A SINGLE COMMA
books.hook: there are no words, only a comma in one exact position.
books.title: A Single Comma
passage: There is a book composed entirely of spaces except for one comma.
The comma occupies an exact position.
In another book it stands one character later. In another, one earlier. To place that single comma in every possible position, a different book is needed each time.
And we have still not written a single word.
books.aftertaste: A different comma. Another complete book.

neighbors.difference: Every character is the same letter.
The combinations eventually form a complete life.

books.headline: ONLY A'S
books.title: Only A's
passage: There is a book in which every character is the letter a.
Another contains only b. Another, only full stops.
Then come the books in which only one character changes: a b among millions of a's, a full stop among spaces, a different letter in the final position.
Every change produces another complete book.
books.aftertaste: Even the most useless book has to exist.

neighbors.difference: Only the position of a comma changes.
The combinations grow readable until they describe a life.

books.headline: UNTIL IT REACHES YOU
books.title: Until It Reaches You
passage: First come the books without words.
Then those that contain one different letter, two, three. Fragments of words appear, unfinished sentences, readable pages and texts that seem to have been written by someone.
Among all those combinations there is also a book that describes your life exactly: your birth, these words and the circumstances of your death.
It was not written for you. It is simply one of the possible combinations.
books.aftertaste: Your book is a combination too.

neighbors.difference: You return to a book with no words, only a comma.
Every character is again the same symbol.
